newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end one percent higher.

text.p: Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher for a second day in a row as index heavyweights Roche, Novartis and Nestle helped the overall market continue its recovery.

U.S. interest rate tightening, which had been expected, had little impact, traders said. They said activity was likely to be quiet on Thursday ahead of the Easter holiday and given the fact that the bourse close will be moved forward to 1300 GMT from 1530 GMT.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 61.9 points, or 1.36 percent, higher at 4,620.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index added 31.15 points to finish at 2,919.11.
Food giant Nestle jumped 4.06 percent, or 64 francs, to 1,641, after it reported a 16.6 percent increase in 1996 group net profit to 3,401 million francs.
Nestle was the only SMI company so far to report 1996 results that were clearly above market expectations, one trader noted.

Dealers said part of today's advance stemmed from short covering in recently pressured stocks. Roche certificates rebounded after Tuesday's weakness, adding 135 francs to end at 12,305, one dealers said.
Novartis registered shares were up 20 to 1,780.
CS Group continued trading with a firmer bias, adding one franc to 174. UBS bears rose three francs to 12.85.
Adecco rose surged 18 francs to 454 after overcoming technical resistance. Surveillance advanced 115 francs to 3,065, in a rebound from a recent sharp fall.
ABB and Electrowatt were uncahnged at 1,700 francs and 533 francs, respectively.
